chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Ali ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
From the misery of living is a narrow home.
ai.seo_question: What is considered a cause of misery in living according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links physical confinement to spiritual and psychological distress, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence which often considers housing adequacy (kifāyah) a component of social well-being. This narration underscores the Islamic emphasis on creating an environment conducive to tranquility (sakinah) and family harmony, reflecting the broader ethical concern for material conditions that support spiritual health.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from Ali Bin Abu Al Mugheira,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘From a miserable living, is a narrow home’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Ibrahim ibn abu al-Balad from Ali ibn abu al-Mughirah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Of the misfortunes in the worldly life is a small and congested house.’”
